I'm hitting a data-correctness bug with a low-cardinality string column after a merge.

*   When a MergeTree table has a LowCardinality(String) column and a merge operation produces multiple dictionaries within a single index granule (because each merge output block overflows the dictionary size limit), the merged part must still store exactly one mark position for the dictionary keys substream — i.e., all dictionary blocks share one mark offset.

*   After the merge described above, querying rows whose values fall in the first dictionary block and rows whose values fall in later dictionary blocks must both return the correct string values — the system must not incorrectly apply only the first dictionary to all rows in the granule.

*   The system must correctly distinguish between a true single-dictionary part (where one dictionary covers all rows and the dictionary stream is exhausted after reading it) and a false-positive case where marks appear uniform but multiple dictionaries were written within a single granule. In the false-positive case, the dictionary must not be cached as a global shared dictionary; instead, dictionary updates must be read from the stream during normal deserialization.

I've implemented the fix. Here's what was wrong and what I changed.

## Root cause

The `single_dictionary_for_part` optimization in `SerializationLowCardinality::deserializeBinaryBulkStatePrefix` uses `has_uniform_marks_callback` to detect a part where one dictionary covers all rows. When marks look uniform, it reads the dictionary once in the prefix, caches it as `global_dictionary`, and sets `single_dictionary_for_part = true` so bulk deserialization never re-reads the dictionary.

The uniform-marks check is **necessary but not sufficient**. When a merge writes several dictionaries *within a single index granule* — because each merge output block overflows `low_cardinality_max_dictionary_size` — the `DictionaryKeys` substream still stores exactly one mark for that granule, so all the dictionary blocks share one mark offset and the marks still appear uniform. The code then cached only the *first* dictionary and, because `single_dictionary_for_part` was true, skipped re-reading the later dictionaries. Rows whose values lived in the second (or later) dictionary block were incorrectly decoded against the first dictionary → wrong string values.

## The fix

After reading the first dictionary in the prefix, I check whether the stream is exhausted (`stream->eof()`):

- **True single-dictionary part** — the keys stream contains only the version plus one dictionary, so it's at EOF. Cache it as the global shared dictionary (unchanged behavior).
- **False positive** — more dictionary data follows, so this is the multi-dict-in-one-granule case. Don't cache a shared dictionary and reset `single_dictionary_for_part = false`, so normal deserialization reads each dictionary update from the stream at its `need_update_dictionary` boundary.

This is safe because the bulk-read path seeks the keys stream back to the granule mark (`seek_to_mark` in `MergeTreeReaderWide::getStream`), so the fallback re-reads all dictionaries from the mark regardless of what the prefix consumed.

I only touched `src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationLowCardinality.cpp`; no test files were modified. Note I did not build/run — a full ClickHouse build is expensive; let me know if you'd like me to build and exercise it.
